clue.text: To walk it needs disturbing measure of power

indicators.note: disturbing the words stirs their letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what strenuous disturbance a walk needs to register on a power meter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word; 'disturbing' is the anagram signal applied to the eight letters of TO WALK IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt, a thousand watts, is a standard unit by which power is measured.

clue.text: Teacher loses head breaking ruler, delivering smack

indicators.note: breaking means the shortened word splits the ruler apart

parts.note: a king is a ruler

indicators.note: loses head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a woman teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher strikes a monarch and delivers a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the first letter of the teacher's title, and 'breaking' splits the ruler round what is left. Smack here means a loud kiss, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack can be a loud kiss, so kissing is delivering one.

clue.text: Last of all, professional goalie to sign

indicators.note: last of all means the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: In the end, a professional goalkeeper signs for the club.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Last of all' seem a separate opening phrase, but it means the last letters of all of professional, goalie and to.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Winder on watch breaking means it's time to get up!

indicators.note: breaking means the pair splits the word for means

parts.note: a way is a means or method

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another is placed above it

parts.note: a key winds a clock or watch
a wake is a watch or vigil kept over a body

explanation.surface: Winding a watch breaks the silence and signals it is time to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' stacks the winder above the watch; 'breaking' then splits the word for means round that pair. A watch here is a vigil, not a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is a jocular call to rouse sleepers in the morning.

clue.text: Body peaks before start of Olympics

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops, peaks

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of Olympics

explanation.surface: Athletes climb peaks before the Olympics begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.

clue.text: Spicy cuisine taken with cold water

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry dish popular in Britain
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A diner pairs a hot curry with a glass of chilled water.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTI is a style of curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, a staple of British curry houses. 'taken with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is a body of water, so the name stands for water in a crossword sense.

clue.text: Strain's affected demeanour

definitions.meaning: strains are melodies or tunes, so taken as a plural noun for tunes
putting on ... means an affected, haughty manner

explanation.definitionFit: Airs are tunes, as strains are, and also pretentious mannerisms.

clue.text: Flick dirt, then ham rolls

indicators.note: rolls means the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flicks dirt off and then rolls up some ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flick' is slang for a film, and The Third Man is the 1949 film noir starring Orson Welles.
explanation.definitionFit: Flick is informal for a film, and this is a classic British film.

clue.text: Subject is mentioned in quote by Newton

indicators.note: in puts the spoken form inside the word for quote

parts.note: to cite is to quote

indicators.note: mentioned means the word is spoken, so spelt as it sounds

parts.note: the word is, as written
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A subject turns up in a quotation by Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: IS 'mentioned' sounds like IZ, which goes 'in' CITE; N is added. 'by' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is a subject of a state, as a Briton is a subject of the Crown.

clue.text: Decline in need of a fall?

definitions.text: Decline in need of a fall?

parts.words: Decline in need of a fall?
parts.note: a downward slope that needs a fall of snow before it can be used

explanation.definitionFit: A slope for skiers is a decline that is useless until snow falls on it.

clue.text: Wealthy neighbourhood family violated right to strike

parts.note: stock means lineage or family descent
broke, as in broke the law, means violated
to belt someone is to strike them hard

explanation.surface: A rich district's family is accused of breaching the workers' right to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The STOCKBROKER BELT is the prosperous commuter area around London, especially Surrey. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an affluent suburban area where well-paid City commuters live.

clue.text: Country squire's first to wear cream-coloured jacket

parts.note: ivory is a creamy off-white colour

indicators.note: the letter is to wear the jacket, so the coat goes round it

parts.note: a coat is an outer garment like a jacket

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of squire's

explanation.surface: A country gentleman's first move is to put on a cream jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory Coast, now officially Côte d'Ivoire, is a West African country.

clue.text: Lower-rent houses for Sgt Lewis maybe here?

definitions.text: Lower-rent houses for Sgt Lewis maybe here?

indicators.note: houses means the pair encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, an ox
to hire is to rent
DS, detective sergeant, was Lewis's rank in Inspector Morse

explanation.surface: Cheap rented homes might suit a detective sergeant in this county.
explanation.walkthrough: OX and HIRE 'house' FOR plus DS. Morse and Lewis worked in Oxford, so the whole clue points to their county.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeant Lewis served with Inspector Morse in Oxford, so the county is where you would find him.

clue.text: Illustrator's sparkle when speaking

definitions.note: read as 'Illustrator is', the definition followed by the link

indicators.note: when speaking signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: fizz is the effervescent sparkle of a drink

explanation.surface: Someone praises an artist's lively spark in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Phiz was the pen name of Hablot K. Browne, illustrator of Dickens's novels. The 's of 'Illustrator's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Phiz is the professional name of the Victorian artist who illustrated Dickens, so he is an illustrator.

clue.text: Falling off cairn's edge when rambling

indicators.note: rambling means the letters wander about into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker tumbles off the rim of a cairn while out rambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' is the anagram signal and 'when' a link word; the surface walker on a cairn's rim hides that the cairn's edge is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling off can mean declining or dwindling, a synonym for growing less.

clue.text: Hot air was freshly made by bellows perhaps

parts.note: guff is empty talk, nonsense or hot air

indicators.note: freshly made says the letters of was are formed anew in another order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the hot air from a bellows was newly produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly made' rearranges WAS into AWS; 'by' is a link word. The surface makes 'bellows' a device for blowing air, but it is the verb meaning roars.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellows, as a verb, means roars loudly, and loud roaring laughs are an example of that.

clue.text: Stone drain concerned with trapping high acidity

indicators.note: trapping means the pair encloses the next piece

parts.note: to sap is to drain of strength
re means about or concerning
pH 1 marks very high acidity, with the figure 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Acid is drawn off a stone, trapping the strong acidity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' puts the acidity inside the drain-plus-about pair. pH 1 is very acidic, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, and stone often means gem.

clue.text: Flood because of leak

parts.note: over can mean on account of, as in a row over money
to run is to leak, as colours run in the wash

explanation.surface: A flood has been caused by a leaking pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to spread over and swamp, as floodwater does to land.

clue.text: Aggressively pass a share of the spoils

definitions.meaning: on the road, to carve someone up is to overtake them dangerously and cut in
a division of loot or gains among the winners

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to overtake recklessly, and the hyphenated noun means a sharing-out of plunder.

clue.text: Impatient chap grabbing maiden cut corner

indicators.note: grabbing means the first piece seizes the second inside it

parts.note: a chafer is one who chafes, fretting impatiently
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A restless fellow grabs a girl and takes a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts the maiden inside the impatient chap. 'cut corner' is a bevelled edge in woodwork, not a shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamfer is a corner or edge cut off at an angle, a bevel.

clue.text: Strasbourg group returned petition, sealing easy success

indicators.note: sealing means the turned word closes round the next piece
returned sends the word for petition back to front

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal formally
a romp is an easy victory

explanation.surface: A European body sends back a petition that had sealed an easy win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the petition backwards, and 'sealing' has it close round the easy success. Euro-MPs are members of the European Parliament, which sits in Strasbourg.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the European Parliament sit in Strasbourg, so they are a group based there.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer is cagey with harsh brief

parts.note: shy and cagey both mean reluctant to commit

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: stern means severe or harsh

explanation.surface: An unscrupulous lawyer is evasive and severe with a legal brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims STERN to STER; 'is' and 'with' are links. The legal sense of brief is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous, disreputable lawyer.

clue.text: Part from one's parents, returning for recess

indicators.note: returning means the extracted run is read backwards
a part taken from the words means a run of letters lifted out of them

explanation.surface: A child leaves the family home and moves away to a quiet spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part from' extracts ESPA from onES PArents, and 'returning' turns it round. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Pal — one working in risky ministerial post

indicators.note: in places the anagram inside the word for risky

parts.note: chancy means uncertain or risky

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A friend is employed in a hazardous government job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns PAL plus I into PLAI, which goes 'in' CHANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplaincy is the office of a chaplain, a minister of religion, so it is a ministerial post.

clue.text: Brief golden age?

definitions.meaning: the best period of life, a personal golden age

explanation.definitionFit: Prime as a verb means to prepare with information, and as a noun the peak period of life.

clue.text: Brave man needing no start to catch second-rate Spanish runner

indicators.note: to catch means the shortened word closes round the next letter
needing no start means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
B is a grade below A, second-rate

explanation.surface: A courageous man without a head start tries to catch a mediocre Spanish athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: HERO 'needing no start' becomes ERO, which goes 'to catch' B. A runner is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of Spain, and runner is crossword shorthand for a river.

clue.text: Fickle chap left one lying around, note, next to tree

indicators.note: around means the liar goes round the letter for left

parts.note: a fibber is someone telling lies
ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
the gibbet, or gallows, was once called a tree

explanation.surface: An unreliable man leaves a liar hanging about, a note pinned to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: FIBBER goes 'around' L to make FLIBBER; 'next to' is a link joining the pieces. Tree for gallows is an old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a flighty, frivolous person, here taken as an unreliable fellow.

clue.text: I disapprove when reserve falls short

indicators.note: falls short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A spectator voices disapproval when the reserve team underperforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls short' trims BOOK to BOO; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is the interjection used to express disapproval or contempt.

clue.text: Returning to eliminate stout African runner

indicators.note: returning means the joined pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: a KO, or knockout, eliminates a boxer
stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A man comes back to cut out stout, said by a runner from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: KO plus BEER is KOBEER; 'Returning' reads it backwards. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok is a southern African antelope, a swift-running animal.

clue.text: Regularly peeping into diary a night-time habit

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A snoop habitually peers into someone's diary at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of peepingintodiary from the first gives the answer. 'habit' is a garment, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light dressing gown, a garment worn at night, and a habit is clothing.
